> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9481bcf3b15ba2e3b00d7c7f6c43276c44a5f187` — the merge of head `e77ad2750539a20766866f78c526b8f78b9d2516` into base `968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9481bcf3b15ba2e3b00d7c7f6c43276c44a5f187 && git checkout 9481bcf3b15ba2e3b00d7c7f6c43276c44a5f187
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925 e77ad2750539a20766866f78c526b8f78b9d2516 && git checkout -B drift-repro 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925 && git merge --no-ff e77ad2750539a20766866f78c526b8f78b9d2516

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 968cacfd10fdec64b6089d0da4f721f1a8a10925` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff changes ONE door, `POST /api/v1/storage/upload/chunked`: after the existing presence check and the existing scope gate, the body is parsed with `InitiateChunkedUploadRequestSchema.safeParse(body)`; a failure answers `sendError(res, 400, 'INVALID_REQUEST', …)` naming each issue as `path: message`; the handler then reads `parsed.data`. Every accept-set change this implies, judged against the schema on `main` (`totalSize: z.number().int().min(1)`, `chunkSize: z.number().int().min(5242880).default(5242880)`, `scope: UploadScopeSchema.default('user')`, `bucket: z.string().optional()`, `metadata: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional()`) and the ruling 6498840027 「Declared is enforced」:

1. `totalSize` must be a whole JSON number ≥ 1 — **right.** `-5`, `"100"`, `0`, `1.5` are refused by name; before, `-5` minted `total_chunks` of `-0`, `"100"` was stored as sent and reached `Math.ceil("100"/5242880)` through `Number(totalSize)`. `0` was already refused (truthiness) under the generic "required" message; it now reaches the parse and is refused as `totalSize: Too small…` — same status and code, a better message.
2. `chunkSize` below 5242880 is refused 400, not clamped — **right**, and exactly the ruling's named behaviour choice. A numeric-string `chunkSize` is refused — right (the clamp's `Math.max("5242880", 5242880)` coerced it). Above the minimum it is honoured unchanged (CONTROL row 10485760 → 2 chunks for 12 000 000 bytes).
3. Omitted `chunkSize` keeps the default — **right.** Zod applies `.default(5242880)` on `undefined`, so `parsed.data.chunkSize` is always a number and `Math.ceil(totalSize / chunkSize)` for a valid body is what `reqChunkSize ?? 5242880` produced before; the CONTROL row pins 12 000 000 → 3 chunks and the stored `chunk_size`. Every in-repo caller omits it or sends 5242880 (see ④), so no existing session shape moves.
4. `chunkSize: null` is refused — **right under the declared schema.** `.default()` is not `.nullable()`; `null` was formerly read as omitted by `??`. This is a narrowing the card did not name but the schema does, and the changeset lists it.
5. `bucket` must be a string when sent; `null` or a non-string is refused — **right** (`z.string().optional()`); before, any type was written to both rows' `bucket`.
6. `metadata` must be an object of string values; `{ tag: 1 }` or `null` is refused — **right** (`z.record(z.string(), z.string()).optional()`); before, any shape was `JSON.stringify`-ed onto both rows and handed to `storage.initiateChunkedUpload(key, { contentType, metadata })`, whose adapters (S3 user metadata) take string values only — so this makes a real refusal real, not a new rule.
7. `scope` — **unchanged accept set.** The gate `requireAcceptedUploadScope(body.scope, res)` runs BEFORE the parse, so an off-vocabulary or retired `public` scope keeps its dedicated remedy text; `null` was and is refused there (`UploadScopeSchema.safeParse(null)` fails). The parse then applies the declared default; `scope ?? 'user'` downstream is now redundant but harmless.
8. Unknown keys — **unchanged**: `z.object` strips them; the handler never read them.
9. Gate order — presence → scope → parse → 413 limit → `createFile` → backend multipart → `createSession`. **Right**: both rows and the backend multipart sit after the parse (the seven REFUSED rows assert `createFile` and `createSession` never called). `requireWithinUploadLimit` now receives a typed number; the `Number(totalSize)` coercion that let a numeric string through is gone.
10. Public surface — **no schema, type, export or error code moves.** `storage.zod.ts` is byte-identical to `main`; the refusal reuses the presigned door's `400 INVALID_REQUEST` envelope from #27537 with the field path in the message; the success body is unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27549-chunked-init-declared-shape.md`: `'@objectstack/service-storage': patch`; line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; BREAKING banner present (`**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing), shipped as patch`); FROM / TO / Fix account present. PR title carries `!`; PR body carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing — …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. `readClause2Line` reads both lines as `{ kind: 'declared', value: 'no', arm: 'narrowing' }` — the arm is the first token inside the parenthesis, so the body's long parenthetical is well-formed.
- Level — **right.** `Metadata-protocol: none` ⇒ `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its banner and disposition (Post-Task Checklist §3). Only `@objectstack/service-storage` publishes a change; `@objectstack/client` and `@objectstack/spec` are untouched.
- ADR-0087 disposition — exactly one marker, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, in an HTML comment. `readDisposition` parses it (`ok: true`, category `no-migration-prescription`); `findMigrationPrescription` on the body returns `null` — the bold `FROM.` / `TO.` / `Fix.` paragraphs are AGENTS.md's required migration account for a breaking changeset, not a `FROM → TO` ledger prescription. **Right in substance too**: no key of any metadata schema, no export, type or error code is removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed. Gate verdict: Check Changeset success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `open_questions: []`. Every flag the dev raised, and the two I add:

- `scope ?? 'user'` now redundant (dev, out-of-scope note) — agreed, cosmetic; no action owed.
- `filename: ''` / `mimeType: ''` refused by the pre-existing presence check although `z.string()` accepts them (dev, Acceptance notes) — a pre-existing declared≠enforced in the STRICTER direction, outside this card; not introduced here. Carrier: none — file-worthy as its own p3 card if the maintainer wants the door to accept exactly the declared set in both directions.
- `null` for `chunkSize` / `bucket` / `metadata` now refused (dev) — judged in ①.4–6: right under the declared schema and the ruling.
- Dev claim "no Console path calls this door" — **verified**: `git grep` under `ui/` at the head finds no `upload/chunked` or `initChunkedUpload` caller.
- Dev claim "the SDK sends the schema's own input type" — **verified**: `packages/client/src/index.ts:5448` `initChunkedUpload(req: InitiateChunkedUploadRequest)`, where `InitiateChunkedUploadRequest` is the `z.input` projection of `InitiateChunkedUploadRequestSchema`; the body is `JSON.stringify(req)`.
- PR body `Skills-docs: none — no skill or doc teaches the old clamp` — **does not hold against the tree**; see ④ should-fix.
- Serial constraint: PR #27537 is merged and the base already carries its presigned parse; the diff applies cleanly on `origin/main` (the three-file diff is identical from the merge-base and from `main`).

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.** Every shape the door now refuses is a shape `InitiateChunkedUploadRequestSchema` on `main` already declares invalid, and the generated reference (`content/docs/references/api/storage.mdx`: `totalSize integer ✅`, `chunkSize integer optional default 5242880`) already told consumers so. The behaviours removed — the 5 MiB clamp, `null`-as-omitted, type-agnostic `bucket` / `metadata`, a coerced numeric-string total — were undeclared leniencies, and the one with a consumer-visible effect (the clamp) silently produced a `totalChunks` different from the one the caller computed; the QA checklist records that very trap. It holds against the ruling (parse with the declared schema; refuse, do not clamp) and against the code it cites: the presigned door's #27537 parse is a hand check because ITS schema declares a bare `z.number()` (part (b), split to `domain:spec`); the init door's schema is already tight, so a whole-schema parse is the right instrument and the two doors answer the same envelope.

Trying to break it at the consumers: every in-repo caller of the init door sends `{ filename, mimeType, totalSize: n ≥ 1 }` as JSON numbers with `chunkSize` omitted or exactly 5242880 — `storage-routes.test.ts`, `chunked-upload-integrity.test.ts`, `chunk-part-record-concurrency.test.ts`, `storage-limits.test.ts`, `storage-routes.metadata-outage.test.ts`, `storage-routes.server-fault-withheld.test.ts`, the success/error-envelope conformance tests, `sys-file-` / `sys-upload-session-organization-stamping.test.ts`, `tenant-audit-update-delete-half-repairs.test.ts`, `upload-door-ownership.test.ts`, `upload-scope-vocabulary.test.ts`; `storage-upload-door-ownership.wall.test.ts` and `storage-upload-organization-change.wall.test.ts` (organizations); `attachments-permission-matrix`, `error-sentences-live`, `storage-chunked-parallel-parts`, `storage-chunked-resume-integrity` (dogfood); `storage-wire-dialect.test.ts` (client, mocked fetch). None sends a body the new parse refuses. The SDK's `resumeUpload(uploadId, file, chunkSize, resumeToken)` takes its chunk size from the caller's own session, not this door. Dogfood Regression Gate and Build Core are green on the head; Test Core shards were still running when read.

Findings:

- **should-fix** — `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/attachments-storage.json` still teaches the removed behaviour in two strings of the upload-session lifecycle item: `steps[0]` ("`chunkSize` is floored at 5 MiB, so a smaller requested value silently yields a different totalChunks than the caller computed") and `source` ("chunkSize = Math.max(reqChunkSize ?? 5242880, 5242880), i.e. a 5 MiB floor"). After this PR a runner following that step is told to expect a clamp and gets a 400. Rewrite both to the refusal (and bump the item's `revision` with a `history` entry, as `check-platform-checklist.mjs` requires). Not a must-fix: the checklist is a QA ledger, not a consumer; no gate reads that prose; the `storage-routes.ts#mimeType` anchor still resolves. May land in this PR or as a follow-up card.
- must-fix — none.
